name: Avery Dennison Corporation
executive_summary: Avery Dennison is a global materials-science and digital-identification business spanning label materials, graphics, tapes and RFID-based intelligent labels, organised into Materials Group (~69% of FY2025 net sales) and Solutions Group (~31%). The quantitative screen flags a buy on cheapness, quality, dividend, GARP and risk metrics (P/E 17.5, FCF yield 6.6%, ROE 30.9%, dividend yield 2.6%), with conviction building at 60% over three weeks. The valuation hook is a high-return, cash-generative franchise trading at a modest earnings multiple after several years of share-price underperformance, whilst management continues to return capital via dividends and buybacks and to bolt on growth (Taylor Adhesives, Wiliot). The central debate is whether Materials Group momentum and productivity savings can offset uneven Solutions Group results—particularly apparel and intelligent labels—plus tariff uncertainty, rising interest expense and a goodwill-heavy balance sheet.
investment_thesis:
For a value investor, AVY combines screen-validated cheapness with business quality that screens alone understate. Seven models pass, spanning FCF Yield, Neff PEGY (0.07), Quality Value, Dividend Growth, Magic Formula, Composite Value and Earnings Quality—five of four required factor families. That breadth suggests the signal is not driven by a single distressed metric; rather, a ~17.5x P/E on a business generating ~6.6% FCF yield and ~31% ROE points to market scepticism rather than fundamental deterioration.

Business quality rests on scale (200+ facilities, 50+ countries, ~35,000 employees), materials-science and converter-channel advantages in Materials Group, and an RFID/intelligent-labels platform in Solutions Group that connects physical and digital supply chains. FY2025 filings describe no single customer above 10% of net sales, R&D expense of $137 million, and restructuring savings exceeding $60 million against $47 million of charges—evidence of an active productivity culture. Capital allocation reinforces the case: the board authorised up to $750 million of repurchases in April 2025, the company bought back 3.2 million shares for $575.6 million in FY2025, and the quarterly dividend was raised to $1.00 in April 2026 (from $0.94). The screen’s buy rating aligns with a compounder trading at a reasonable absolute and sector-relative (67%) valuation, not a deep cyclical trough.
financial_review:
**Annual results (10-K, filed 25 February 2026)**

The FY2025 and FY2024 10-K body extracts in the library are truncated before Item 8 financial statements; consolidated income-statement totals below therefore fall back to `financials_annual.json` (Yahoo). Filing-body content is used for balance-sheet, capital-allocation and narrative items where present.

| Metric | FY2025 (Yahoo fallback) | FY2024 (Yahoo fallback) | Change |
|--------|---------------------------|-------------------------|--------|
| Net sales | $8,855.5m | $8,755.7m | +1.1% |
| Net income | $688.0m | $704.9m | −2.4% |
| Diluted EPS | $8.79 | $8.73 | +0.7% |
| Operating income | $1,123.8m | $1,115.4m | +0.8% |
| Free cash flow | $681.0m | $699.0m | −2.6% |
| Operating cash flow | $881.4m | $938.8m | −6.1% |

From the FY2025 10-K narrative (filing body): total debt was approximately **$3.73 billion** at 31 December 2025; average borrowings ~$739 million; the company repurchased **3.2 million shares for $575.6 million**; acquired W.F. Taylor Holdings (Taylor Adhesives) for ~**$390 million**; incurred **~$47 million** of restructuring charges with incremental savings exceeding **$60 million**; capital expenditure ~**$200 million**. International operations represented ~**69%** of net sales. No going-concern qualification appears in available extracts.

Earnings dipped slightly in FY2025 despite modest top-line growth, consistent with higher interest expense, growth investment and tax/discrete items visible in interim filings. Normalised income (Yahoo) was ~$746 million versus reported $688 million, reflecting ~$78 million of unusual items.

**Interim results (10-Q filings — primary source)**

*Q1 2026 (period ended 31 March 2026, filed 5 May 2026):*
- Net sales **$2,298.5m** (+7% reported; **+1% organic**); net income **$168.1m**; diluted EPS **$2.18** (vs $2.09 prior year).
- Adjusted free cash flow **$104.4m** (vs −$53.1m in Q1 2025, when working-capital timing was adverse).
- Materials Group net sales **$1,649.3m** (+11% reported, **+2% organic**); segment adjusted operating income **$254.2m**.
- Solutions Group net sales **$649.2m** (−3% reported, **−1% organic**); segment adjusted operating income **$58.5m** (down from $68.2m); intelligent labels down low single digits organically.
- Total debt **$3.79 billion**; shareholders’ equity **$2.30 billion**; company in compliance with revolver leverage covenant.

*Q3 2025 (period ended 27 September 2025):*
- Q3 net sales **$2,215.5m**; Q3 net income **$166.3m**; diluted EPS **$2.13**.
- Nine-month net sales **$6,584.3m** (flat YoY); nine-month net income **$521.6m** (vs $530.9m); nine-month adjusted FCF **$404.5m** (vs $420.0m).
- Nine-month Materials Group segment adjusted operating income **$702.9m**; Solutions Group **$204.9m** (both down slightly YoY).

*Q2 2025 (period ended 28 June 2025):*
- Q2 net sales **$2,220.5m**; Q2 net income **$189.0m**; H1 net sales **$4,368.8m**; H1 net income **$355.3m**.

**Trend assessment:** Top-line growth is low single digits organically, with reported figures boosted by FX and acquisitions (Taylor Adhesives). Profitability is resilient but not expanding—FY2025 net income edged lower, nine-month 2025 earnings trailed prior year, yet Q1 2026 showed stabilisation with volume-driven Materials growth. Cash conversion improved sharply in Q1 2026 (operating cash flow $136.5m vs −$16.3m prior year). Interest expense is rising (Q1 2026: $35.6m vs $30.9m), linked to higher commercial-paper balances and September 2025 euro note issuance. **Gap:** full-year FY2025 consolidated statements are not available in filing-body extracts; Yahoo figures should be cross-checked against the 10-K tables before trading.
risks_and_flags:
**Macro / cyclical:** The 10-K and subsequent 10-Q risk-factor updates emphasise tariff and trade-policy uncertainty. Management estimated an aggregate **low single-digit rate decrease in apparel-category sales** in Q2–Q4 2025 from indirect tariff impacts. Packaging-sector commentary in the news flow (BofA, July 2026) points to lacklustre demand and weak volumes—relevant to label end-markets.

**Segment divergence:** Solutions Group adjusted operating income fell in Q1 and Q3 2025 and Q1 2026, with apparel/base business soft whilst high-value categories grow unevenly. Intelligent-label growth slowed to low single digits in recent quarters—not a broken thesis, but a deceleration the screen may not capture.

**Balance sheet / leverage:** Total debt ~$3.7–3.8 billion against equity ~$2.2–2.3 billion; goodwill **$2.26 billion** and acquisition intangibles **$801 million** at Q1 2026 leave **negative tangible book value** (Yahoo: −$858 million at FY2025). The revolver contains a **maximum leverage-ratio covenant**; the company reported compliance at each interim date. A credit-rating downgrade could constrain commercial-paper access (disclosed in 10-K).

**Pension / employee benefits:** Accumulated other comprehensive loss includes **$49.2 million** of pension/post-retirement obligations at Q1 2026—modest relative to scale but flagged as a risk factor.

**Operational / credit:** In January 2026, a large Materials Group customer filed for **prepackaged Chapter 11** protection; management stated it expects to collect prepetition receivables, but widespread customer stress would be material. Restructuring continues (~370 positions in Q1 2026 alone; ~$15.9 million charges).

**Legal / environmental:** The company is a PRP at **ten** EPA/state hazardous-waste sites; environmental liability accrual ~$9.6 million at Q1 2026. Legal proceedings are described as routine with no individually material expected impact, though outcomes could differ from accruals.

**Governance / insider activity:** News reports an executive chairman share sale associated with an ~11% stock drop in March 2026—worth monitoring but not, on its own, a fundamental red flag.

**Other:** Venture-investment losses ($1.3 million Q1 2026; $14.3 million Q1 2025) add earnings volatility. No going-concern language identified. Eight of eighteen indexed 8-K filings lack body extracts, limiting event-level verification.
news_highlights:

**Earnings and capital returns**

- *Avery Dennison Increases Quarterly Dividend* (Business Wire, 30 April 2026); *Avery Dennison Sets Sept. 16 Payment for $1 Dividend* (Stock Titan, 23 July 2026) — dividend raised to **$1.00/quarter** (~6% increase).
- *The Bull Case For Avery Dennison (AVY) Could Change Following Dividend Hike And Capital Return Push* (Yahoo Finance, 4 May 2026).

**Strategy / management / M&A**
- *Avery Dennison Names Danny Allouche President, Materials Group* (Business Wire, 4 June 2026) — leadership change in core segment.
- *Will Avery Dennison’s New Materials Chief Recast Its RFID and Sustainability Story for Investors (AVY)?* (simplywall.st, 7 July 2026).
- *AVY Debuts Clima Series in India for Solar Control & Energy Efficiency* (Yahoo Finance, 11 June 2026) — product/geographic expansion.
- Q1 2026 10-Q notes a subsequent **~$75 million minority investment in Wiliot Ltd.** (27 April 2026) to expand sensor/supply-chain technology.

**Sector / sentiment**
- *Packaging, Forest Products Face Lackluster Demand, Weak Volumes, BofA Says* (Yahoo Finance, 14 July 2026) — sector headwind context.
- *Avery Dennison (AVY) On The Smart Labels Narrative And Its Undervalued View* (Yahoo Finance, 11 July 2026); *Avery Dennison: Hold For Now, Due To Uneven Segment Results* (Seeking Alpha, 13 May 2026) — debate on whether RFID narrative is fully priced.
- *AVY Stock Falls -11% On Executive Chairman’s Share Sale Amid Sector Weakness* (Trefis, 11 March 2026).

**Valuation commentary:** Multiple GuruFocus/Yahoo pieces cite GF Value above spot price (e.g. *GF Value Says Undervalued*, 24 July 2026), though these are model-driven and should not substitute for filing-based work.
research_rationale: Deep research broadly confirms the screen’s buy case—durable cash generation, shareholder returns and reasonable multiples—but uneven Solutions Group performance, tariff/trade overhang, rising leverage and truncated annual filing extracts prevent full conviction until FY statements are reconciled from the complete 10-K.
